name: Building a Water Secure Future: World Bank Group Water Strategy (FY25-30)
description: The World Bank Group corporate water sector strategy for FY2025-30, setting three pillars - Water for People, Water for Food, Water for Planet - with strategic objectives and a section on enabling private sector participation and commercial financing.
quick_insights: Core focus areas include restoring rivers and aquifers, wastewater treatment and reuse, river clean-up and pollution management, basin-level planning, and dam safety. Private-sector levers named: hybrid PPPs for wastewater treatment and reuse, sustainability-linked and catastrophe bonds, green securitization, catchment funds, pooled risk facilities, carbon market linkages, parametric insurance, and performance-based contracts for early warning and hydromet equipment.

name: World Bank Group Water Strategy Implementation Plan: Water Forward
description: The implementation plan for the World Bank Group water strategy, published December 2025. Sets targets, segments clients, and defines seven scalable solutions with three enablers.
quick_insights: Target: improve water security for 400 million people by 2030 through seven scalable solutions. States 2.1 billion people lack safely managed drinking water and more than 3.4 billion live without adequate sanitation (JMP 2025); 4 billion experience water scarcity every year. Water-dependent economic sectors provide 1.7 billion jobs worldwide, roughly half of all jobs globally. Solutions span urban water and sanitation service optimization, rural water supply and sanitation, bankable investments for water, wastewater, reuse and desalination, farmer-led and centralized irrigation, flood and drought risk reduction, and restoration of rivers and aquifers.

name: Mainstreaming Water Resilience in Asia and the Pacific: Guidance Note
description: Asian Development Bank operational guidance for scaling up and mainstreaming resilience in ADB water sector operations, structured around six mutually reinforcing pillars. Published July 2022.
quick_insights: Frames Asia and the Pacific as the most disaster-prone region in the world, and water as the primary medium through which climate change impacts are felt. Builds on ADB portfolio analysis and on the Independent Evaluation Department thematic evaluation of ADB Support for Action on Climate Change 2011-2020, which identified deficiencies in ADB climate action. Parallel initiatives named as of April 2022: cluster technical assistance on Mainstreaming Water Resilience, the Asia and the Pacific Water Resilience Hub, and the RUWR "aRe yoU Water Resilient?" initiative.

name: Aqueduct 4.0: Updated decision-relevant global water risk indicators
description: World Resources Institute technical note documenting the Aqueduct 4.0 water risk framework: the hydrological model, future projections, indicator definitions, country and state aggregation, and stated limitations. Underpins the Aqueduct Water Risk Atlas and Country Rankings tools.
quick_insights: Curates 13 water risk indicators spanning quantity, quality and reputational concerns, each sourced from an open-source peer-reviewed data provider. The Aqueduct platform has been running since 2011. The note carries an explicit Limitations section.
